title: fraud_detection Module
content_markdown: This module provides a way to prevent some basic fraud attacks. Alerts are provided through return codes and events.
overview: This module provides a way to prevent some basic fraud attacks. Alerts are provided through return codes and events.
how_it_works:
Basically, this module watches the following parameters:

*   Total calls
    
*   Calls per minute
    
*   Concurrent calls
    
*   Number of sequential calls
    
*   Call duration
    
Each of the above parameters is monitored for every user and every called prefix separately. The stats are altered whenever the _check_fraud_ function is called. The function assumes a new call is made, and checks the called number against all the rules from the supplied profile. The rule's prefix is considered to be the called prefix which along with the provided user will be used to monitor values for the 5 parameters.

A rule is a set of two thresholds (warning and critical thresholds) for each of the five parameters (as described above) and is only available for a specified prefix. Further more, a rule will only match between the indicated hours in the indicated days of the week (similarly to a dr rule). A fraud profile is simply a group of fraud rules and is used to only to limit the list of rules to match when calling the check_fraud function.

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: Database where to load the rules from.
exported_parameters.notes: At least one db_url should be defined for the fraud_detection module to work.

exported_parameters.name: use_utc_time
exported_parameters.description: Set this parameter to non-zero in order to enable UTC-based interval matching and statistics resets, rather than local time-based.

exported_parameters.name: table_name
exported_parameters.description: If you want to load the rules from the database you must set this parameter as the database name.

exported_parameters.name: rid_col
exported_parameters.description: The column's name in the database storing the fraud rule's id.

exported_parameters.name: pid_col
exported_parameters.description: The column's name in the database storing the fraud profile's id. Please keep in mind that a profile is merely a set of rules.
exported_parameters.notes: Please keep in mind that a profile is merely a set of rules.

exported_parameters.name: prefix_col
exported_parameters.description: The column's name in the database storing the prefix for which the fraud rule will match.

exported_parameters.name: start_h
exported_parameters.description:
The column's name in the database storing the the start time of the interval in which the rule will match.

The time needs to be specified as string using the format: “HH:MM”

exported_parameters.name: end_h
exported_parameters.description:
The column's name in the database storing the the end time of the interval in which the rule will match.

The time needs to be specified as string using the format: “HH:MM”

exported_parameters.name: days_col
exported_parameters.description:
The column's name in the database storing the week days in which the fraud rule's interval is available.

The daysoftheweek needs to be specified as a string containing a list of days or intervals. Each day must be specified using the first three letters of its name. A valid string would be: "Fri-Mon, Wed, Thu"

exported_functions.name: check_fraud

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: the user who is making the call. Please keep in mind that the user doesn't have to be registered. This string is only used to keep different stats for different registered users.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: the number the user is calling to.

parameters.name: profile_id
parameters.description: the fraud profile id (i.e. the subset of fraud rules) in which to try and find a matching fraud rule.

return_values.condition: no matching fraud rule was found
a matching rule was found, but there is no parameter above the rule's threshlod, i.e - everything is ok
there is a parameter above the warning threshold value. Check the raised event for more info
there is a parameter above the critical threshold value. Check the raised event for more info

exported_functions.description:
This method should be called each time a given _user_ calls a given _number_. It will try to match a fraud rule within the given fraud profile and update the stats (see above). Furthermore, the stats will be checked against the rule's thresholds. If any of the stats is above its threshold value, the appropriate event will also be raised (see further details below).

Designed to only work with initial INVITE messages! If a dialog is not already present, one will be created (equivalent of create\_dialog()).

exported_mi_functions.name: show_fraud_stats
exported_mi_functions.description: Show the current statistics for all dials of a _user_ to a _prefix_. NOTE: Since the fraud statistics are refreshed on-the-fly, as check\_fraud() is called, **this function will return stale data** if check\_fraud() has not been called at least once for the (user, prefix) pair within a newly matching time interval!

exported_mi_functions.name: fraud_reload
exported_mi_functions.description: Reload the all the fraud rules.
